stories.statLabel: people killed on the first day
stories.headline: Israel launches first ground push in Gaza since the ceasefire
body: Israeli forces began a new operation in central Gaza, the first broad ground offensive since a ceasefire was signed over a year ago.
At least three Palestinians were killed, hospital officials said.
Many people fled areas near the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps.
stories.vc: Renewed fighting threatens aid deliveries and rebuilding plans.

image.credit: WAFA in contract with a local company (APAimages)‏‏ / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Hakeem Jeffries nominated as first Black US House speaker
body: Democrats chose Hakeem Jeffries as their nominee for speaker of the US House.
He is the first Black lawmaker formally nominated for the role.
Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in this month's midterms.
stories.joke: The gavel has a new favourite.
stories.vc: A Democratic House changes the outlook for tax, trade and tech bills.

stories.headline: Ukraine knocks out part of the Crimea bridge
body: Ukraine hit the bridge linking Russia to Crimea with heavy drones and cruise missiles in two waves.
One arch collapsed, cutting car traffic and leaving trains with one track.
Kyiv spent weeks knocking out the air defences guarding it first.
stories.vc: Cutting Crimea's main supply link raises Russia's military and trade costs.

stories.headline: Ribbit Capital sells 1.4% of Groww for ₹1,905 crore
body: US investor Ribbit Capital sold 8.7 crore Groww shares at ₹219 each in block deals.
Buyers included funds tied to BlackRock and Fidelity, and Kotak Mahindra MF.
Ribbit has raised about ₹7,871 crore from Groww's IPO and later sales.
stories.vc: Big VCs cashing out of listed startups shows the IPO route is paying off.

stories.headline: Humyn Labs raises $47M to gather training data for robots
body: Physical-AI startup Humyn Labs raised $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in debt.
It says it crossed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months.
It will expand to Brazil, South Korea and India; Jump Trading also invested.
stories.joke: Teaching robots, one dataset at a time.
stories.vc: Robot makers' hunger for data is a new export business for India.

stories.headline: Higher pensions for 4.45 lakh people may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore
body: EPFO says paying higher pensions under a Supreme Court ruling could cost an extra ₹1.109 lakh crore.
It has sent demand letters to 4.45 lakh applicants.
Pension orders have gone to about 1.52 lakh people so far.
stories.joke: Retirement maths just got a lot harder.
stories.vc: A big bill could pressure EPFO's finances and future returns.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83, above the range
body: Anthropic reportedly priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70–78 range.
That values it at $1.5 trillion fully diluted.
It starts trading on Nasdaq on Thursday as 'ANT'. (No new FT/Unhedged piece, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Ticker ANT, valuation very much not ant-sized.
stories.vc: A strong debut would show investors still trust the AI boom after Nvidia's turmoil.

image.credit: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Payhawk raises $280M led by Goldman Sachs
body: UK fintech Payhawk raised a $280 million Series C at a $2 billion valuation.
Goldman Sachs' growth equity arm led the round.
It uses AI agents to help companies manage spending in 33 countries. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's deal.)
stories.joke: Expense reports, now with fewer tears.
stories.vc: Europe's fintechs are drawing big rounds again.

stories.headline: Nvidia's startup stakes hit $65.5B, but future deals are in doubt
body: Nvidia says its stakes in private companies are now worth $65.5 billion, up from $22 billion in January.
It invested $16 billion in equities last quarter alone.
It's unclear if the deal spree continues without Jensen Huang.
stories.joke: The biggest VC in AI might be a chip company.
stories.vc: AI startups that relied on Nvidia money may need new backers.

stories.statLabel: Ben Thompson's verdict on Nvidia's results
stories.headline: Stratechery: Nvidia's dull results show Huang probably isn't coming back
body: Ben Thompson calls Nvidia's earnings boring.
He argues they explain why Jensen Huang probably won't return.
He also looks at rival Microsoft and Anthropic operating-system updates.
stories.vc: Steady results reduce pressure on the board to bring Huang back.

image.credit: Thor Brødreskift  /  Nordiske Mediedager / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Nvidia delays its routine 10-Q filing, and offers no reason
body: Nvidia says it will file its detailed quarterly report, the 10-Q, 'in the coming weeks' instead of with its results.
It usually files the same day.
The 10-Q includes legal proceedings and risk factors. (No checkable Economist piece today, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: The homework is late, and the class is noticing.
stories.vc: Filing delays can spook investors already worried about legal risks.

stories.headline: Mary Peltola will be the first Alaska Native in the US Senate
body: Democrat Mary Peltola has won an Alaska Senate seat, beating Republican Dan Sullivan.
She will be the first Alaska Native elected to the Senate.
She was also the first Alaska Native in the US House, in 2022.
stories.joke: Two firsts, one very busy résumé.
stories.vc: Her focus on fishing and energy matters to Alaska's economy.

stories.headline: Marines who reported sexual assault were later kicked out
body: At least 30 Marines were discharged in five years after reporting they were sexually assaulted, records show.
The War Horse investigation was republished by The 19th.
One officer trainee says she was assaulted at a Marine Corps ball in 2023.
stories.vc: Survivor protections affect recruitment and retention in the military.

stories.statLabel: India conference of Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians
stories.headline: Shivakumar hopes Parliament passes women's reservation this winter
body: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar hopes the Women's Reservation Bill passes in Parliament's winter session.
He spoke after opening the first India conference of Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians.
The event was held at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru.
stories.vc: More women lawmakers could shift spending on health and childcare.

stories.headline: Tiruchy government hospital to open 600-bed block on Nov 20
body: CM C. Joseph Vijay will open a new 600-bed super speciality building at Tiruchy's MGM Government Hospital on November 20.
It has seven floors and about 2.1 lakh sq ft; costs rose from ₹110 crore to ₹134 crore.
Patients from Karur, Perambalur, Ariyalur and Pudukkottai also use the hospital.
stories.joke: Six hundred beds and zero waiting-room jokes.
stories.vc: More public beds ease crowding in one of central Tamil Nadu's busiest hospitals.

stories.headline: Sikkim opens a 14-bed medical ICU at STNM Hospital
body: Sikkim CM Prem Singh Tamang opened a 14-bed medical intensive care unit at STNM Hospital, Sochakgang.
It was built through Sun Pharma's CSR programme.
It will provide specialised critical care.
stories.joke: More ICU beds, fewer long journeys.
stories.vc: Corporate CSR is helping fill critical-care gaps in smaller states.

stories.headline: Apollo opens in Gurugram with a 90-minute doctor-at-home service
body: Apollo Homecare launched a doctor-at-home pilot in Gurugram alongside the opening of Apollo Hospitals Gurgaon.
It promises a doctor within 90 minutes, for a flat ₹3,500 fee.
It covers non-emergency needs like fever and chronic-condition check-ups.
stories.joke: House calls are back, with an app.
stories.vc: Home visits feed patients into the chain's new hospital.

stories.headline: 24X files to launch an options market with KPI 'binary' bets
body: 24X National Exchange has asked the SEC to approve a new options market, 24X Options.
It would list normal stock options plus yes-or-no options on whether companies hit targets like revenue or EPS.
The KPI contracts would start with 23 heavily traded US stocks.
stories.joke: Will they beat earnings? Now there's a contract for that.
stories.vc: More venues and new contracts mean more work for market makers.

stories.headline: Prop firm boss says no to prediction markets as regulators close in
body: Select Vantage CEO Daniel Schlaepfer plans a 'Real Trading' platform without prediction markets.
The CFTC warned this week that bets on what famous people say carry high manipulation risk.
Global prediction-market volume still hit about $50.6 billion in July.
stories.joke: Trading, not betting. Apparently there's a difference.
stories.vc: Tighter rules on event contracts could slow a fast-growing product for brokers.

stories.headline: Explainer: what is a binary option, or event contract?
body: A binary option pays a fixed amount if something happens, and nothing if it doesn't.
24X wants to list ones on whether companies hit revenue or EPS targets.
Unlike owning a stock, there's no in-between: you're either right or you lose your stake.
stories.vc: Simple to understand, easy to lose: why regulators watch these closely.

stories.headline: Cadillac keeps Bottas for 2027 instead of promoting Herta
body: Cadillac will keep Valtteri Bottas alongside Sergio Pérez for the 2027 F1 season.
The team decided not to fast-track American test driver Colton Herta.
Bottas had struggled for pace against Pérez this year.
stories.joke: Experience wins the seat, for now.
stories.vc: Two veterans give F1's newest team stability as it builds.
